sections.what_happened: Container carriers are restarting Red Sea services amid reduced Ansar Allah attacks on shipping: AP Moller-Maersk confirms an India-via-Middle East-to-US reefer service via the Red Sea; Red Sea Container Terminals opened Egypt's first semiautomated facility at Sokhna Port. Journal of Commerce: the Suez east-west shipment share is 18.7%, near the two-year average, vs ~80% pre-disruption. BUT volatility: CMA CGM announced some Asia-Europe services (FAL1, FAL3, MEX) that transited Suez in 2025 will go back via the Cape of Good Hope, citing a 'complex and uncertain international context' and renewed Ansar Allah attack threats in January 2026. Al Arabiya Business (Threads, Oct 21): Hapag-Lloyd regional president Juan Pablo Richards said more services would return via Bab el-Mandeb/Suez after meeting Suez Canal Authority chairman Osama Rabie. PORTWATCH: Bab el-Mandeb 7d avg 26.43 transits/day vs 2025 baseline 33.47 (79% of baseline); latest observation 32 transits (17 tankers) on 2026-10-18; snapshot NOT stale.
sections.what_verified: Maersk confirmation is primary-source (company's own service); CMA CGM announcement primary-source. The 18.7% figure is via Journal of Commerce (no declared tier -- attribution only). assafinaonline has no declared tier. Hapag-Lloyd via Al Arabiya Threads graphic (Arabic; attribution only).
sections.what_disputed: CMA CGM's reversal (FAL1/FAL3/MEX back to the Cape) shows the return is fragile, not settled. The Suez 18.7% figure comes from one trade publication citing JoC. PortWatch shows Bab el-Mandeb at 79% of baseline, not back to normal -- 'reopening' is carriers' scheduling, not traffic reality. Ansar Allah yacht incident (Oct 22, covered) and Jan-2026 threat warnings are the live risk.
sections.why_matters: The world's biggest container lines are quietly sailing back into the Red Sea -- but one giant just turned its ships around again. The 18.7% number, and why the 'reopening' is not what it sounds like.
sections.context: Background: NEW -- Red Sea shipping reopening: container carriers restarting services (Maersk confirms India-ME-US reefer run); CMA CGM pulls FAL1/FAL3/MEX back to Cape of Good Hope; Suez east-west share 18.7% vs ~80% pre-disruption (Journal of Commerce)

The 18.7% number, and why the 'reopening' is not what it sounds like.
